protections: P1 (CWE-862): state-changing legacy @@API routes must check that the caller may change the target object (AccessJSONAPI, or the field/transition/delete permission on that object) before acting; at the pinned commit only /create checks it (src/bika/lims/jsonapi/create.py:178-182).

P2 (CWE-95): record values sent as strings must be parsed as data literals and never evaluated as code; at the pinned commit both the JSON API (src/bika/lims/jsonapi/__init__.py:237-240) and the field layer (src/senaite/core/browser/fields/record.py:253-256, records.py:138-140) call eval() on them. The screener assumed this half was already fixed; it is not in the pinned tree, and src/senaite/core/browser/fields/parsing.py does not exist.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the docstring calls update_many a wrapper around update (update.py:185-186), so fixing update() seems to cover it, but it does its own restrictedTraverse lookup and calls set_fields_from_request directly
deletion looks as if it is already guarded by the container's 'Delete objects' check inside manage_delObjects, and remove never touches the eval/field sink
portal_workflow.doActionFor already enforces transition guards for the current user, so an extra API gate looks redundant

the field layer is outside the JSON API that the report names, and the jsonapi eval looks like the only sink; but the exact class-path match at __init__.py:237-238 skips every RecordField/RecordsField subclass (AddressField, IDFormattingField, ...), so their raw strings reach the field's own eval through the mutator
read is the read-only route that every user's UI depends on, and the fix is framed around state-changing routes
a gate placed in the per-object loop looks complete, but read() has already run caller-named methods (include_methods) on every match before the loop starts
it only reads user ids and full names and changes nothing
it only lists transitions that getTransitionsFor already filters by the caller's own guards
a planted extra IRouteProvider (for example a remarks-only or batch route) looks like a neighbouring feature, not one of the routes named in the report

masking: None in the strict sense: the eval sinks (T7/T8) and the missing gates (T1-T4, T11) are reachable independently at the pinned commit. One interaction: a gate on update/update_many (T1/T2) shrinks the set of callers who can reach T7, but it does not close T7, and T8 can also be reached by any code path that hands a string to a RecordField subclass mutator.

conflicts.what: Gating @@API/update with AccessJSONAPI (LabManager/Manager only, rolemap.xml:612-615) breaks remarks posting, which the remarks widget does through @@API/update (remarkswidget.js:158-165) and which Analyst, Client, LabClerk, Publisher, Sampler and Verifier are allowed to do (rolemap.xml:514-523).

Gating @@API/read (or the whole @@API view) to close include_methods breaks the cached jsonapi_read and remarks fetch that every logged-in user relies on (senaite.core.common.js:117-121, remarkswidget.js:136-142); the fix has to restrict include_methods, not read.

Replacing eval with json.loads breaks the Python-literal record strings the project's own doctest sends (single-quoted dict at update.py:74 into AddressField PostalAddress); the safe parser has to accept Python literals (ast.literal_eval-style), and the same must apply in RecordField.set.

fairness_risks: If hidden tests require a non-manager's @@API/update to be refused outright, that contradicts the remarks widget, which posts remarks through @@API/update for Analyst/Client/LabClerk etc. (remarkswidget.js:158-165, rolemap.xml:514-523). The tests must either allow a field-level-permission fix or exempt remarks, and must not require both 'Analyst update denied' and 'Analyst remarks work'.
Refused input shape that legitimate use needs: single-quoted Python dict literals for record fields (update.py:74 doctest). A JSON-only parser would refuse them.
@@API/read must stay reachable by every authenticated user (senaite.core.common.js:117-121); a hidden test for T9 must target include_methods, not read access itself.

T12 (allowedTransitionsFor_many) and T11 (getusers) are read-only and may not be a real vulnerability under a reasonable security model; a test requiring them to be closed would penalise a defensible solver judgement.

design.why: Five independent groups, each needing its own judgement and each with a different reason to dismiss: T2 is dismissed as 'just a wrapper' (M1, deepseek); T4 because workflow guards look sufficient (M4, xhard for DeepSeek); T5 is the coupled remarks write that an over-broad AccessJSONAPI gate breaks (M11, mimo); T8 is the second eval in the field layer, reached because an exact type-name match skips subclasses (M2, deepseek+how-type); T9 is include_methods on the must-keep-working read route (M4 plus a coupled value, both types). T1/T7 are left as the easy, report-described anchors. The design covers both protections (P1 and P2), includes the required deepseek-type and mimo-type traps, and has three built-in conflicts (T1-T5, T9-T6, T7-T8), so blanket gating fails. Dropped: T11/T12 because they are read-only and contestable; T10 because it shares its fix with T9; T3 because its strength depends on unverified manage_delObjects behaviour.
